title: Pin the Rust toolchain and tighten empty-collection assertions
summary: This change adds a rust-toolchain.toml pinning the workspace to Rust 1.99.0 with clippy and rustfmt, and rewrites a broad set of test assertions across the osf and osf-lint-core crates from `assert!(x.is_empty())` to `assert_eq!(x, Vec::<T>::new())`. The production code paths are untouched: the diff is a toolchain pin plus assertion-style churn in the writing lints, work-item reference scanner, config loader, reviewer roster, moon report parser, agent registry and changeset-risk tests.

nodes.label: rust-toolchain.toml
nodes.subtitle: channel 1.99.0, minimal, clippy + rustfmt
nodes.summary: New workspace-level toolchain pin. Every cargo, clippy and rustfmt invocation in the repository now resolves to Rust 1.99.0 with the minimal profile and the clippy and rustfmt components, instead of whatever toolchain the developer or CI happened to have active.

nodes.label: cargo / rustup
nodes.subtitle: build, test, clippy, fmt
nodes.summary: The build driver that reads rust-toolchain.toml before compiling anything. Unchanged itself, but its resolved compiler version is now fixed by the new pin.

nodes.label: osf
nodes.subtitle: lint engine, config, reviewers, work items
nodes.summary: The main crate. Its production modules — writing lints, work-item reference scanning, config loading, reviewer roster, moon report parsing, agent registry, changeset risk — are not modified; only their test modules changed.

nodes.label: osf-lint-core
nodes.subtitle: expectation checking
nodes.summary: The shared lint-core crate. Its expectation checker is untouched; only the test module's empty-vector assertions were rewritten.

nodes.label: writing lint tests
nodes.subtitle: rules_of(...) empty-result assertions
nodes.summary: The largest cluster of rewrites. Every `assert!(rules_of(...).is_empty())` became `assert_eq!(rules_of(...), Vec::<&str>::new())`, covering bare references, chat-local references, capitalised-word heuristics, contractions, bold sentences and processor-architecture names.

nodes.label: work-item reference tests
nodes.subtitle: candidates_both(...) empty-result assertions
nodes.summary: Rewrites in the reference-candidate tests: prose numbers, HTML entities, tilde fences, unindented fences, inline code spans, HTML comments and block quotes now assert equality against an empty Vec<Reference>.

nodes.label: config loader tests
nodes.subtitle: must_explain_names / known_names / reviewers
nodes.summary: Rewrites in the config tests, asserting empty writing-name lists and an empty reviewer list via equality against Vec::<String>::new().

nodes.label: reviewer roster tests
nodes.subtitle: roster and sandbox_check
nodes.summary: Unit and integration rewrites around the reviewer roster: an empty roster and an empty sandbox_check are now compared against typed empty vectors.

nodes.label: moon report tests
nodes.subtitle: parse_report / parse_query_tasks
nodes.summary: Two rewrites: a non-empty task list is asserted with assert_ne! against an empty Vec<TaskOutcome>, and an empty query result with assert_eq! against an empty Vec<TaskSlot>.

nodes.label: agent registry tests
nodes.subtitle: name and env emptiness
nodes.summary: Rewrites in the agent registry tests: an empty name becomes assert_ne!(a.name, "") and empty env lists become equality against &[].

nodes.label: changeset risk tests
nodes.subtitle: signals_for empty result
nodes.summary: A single rewrite: an empty risk-signal list is now compared against Vec::<String>::new().

nodes.label: expectation checker tests
nodes.subtitle: missing / unexpected emptiness
nodes.summary: Rewrites in osf-lint-core: empty missing and unexpected lists from the expectation checker are now compared against typed empty vectors.

nodes.label: scan rules integration tests
nodes.subtitle: rule_ids(...) empty-result assertions
nodes.summary: Integration rewrites: plain text, repository-relative paths, missing-owner rules, denylist misses and normal commit messages now assert equality against an empty Vec<&str> of rule ids.

edges.label: resolves channel 1.99.0
edges.summary: The one genuinely new runtime relationship: cargo and rustup now read the workspace toolchain pin before building, so the compiler version is fixed for every crate in the workspace.
